correctness.rationale: Independently re-verified from matrix entries without trusting candidate code. M* row sums and column sums are all 3. Brute-force definition expansion over 720 permutations gives per(M*)=17; independent Ryser evaluation gives 17; all 64 certificate Ryser terms (rowsums, products, signs) recomputed exactly and sum to 17. From-scratch pruned row-by-row backtracking over 20 weight-3 patterns reproduced |D(6,3)|=297200 (matching OEIS A001501 a(6)). Independent vectorized Ryser over all 297200 matrices reproduced the 4-value distribution 17:21600, 18:216000, 20:59400, 36:200 summing to 297200, so the minimum 17 is exhaustive, not sampled. Spot brute-force checks on random samples of each value agreed. Canonical key (lexicographically minimal sorted row-mask tuple over all 720 column permutations, row order quotiented by sorting) showed all 21600 minimizers share one key, i.e. one orbit under independent row/column permutations; direct S_6 x S_6 orbit enumeration of M* gives orbit size 21600 and stabilizer 518400/21600=24. Schrijver bound (4/3)^6~=5.619 (ceil 6) and ratio 17*729/4096=12393/4096~=3.026 verified; Bregman consistency holds (max 36). Evidence is computational-exhaustive (proof by complete finite enumeration with replayable certificates), honestly presented as such, not an analytic proof.

originality.rationale: Nearest priors compared substantively, not by timestamp. OEIS A001501 records only the count |D(n,3)| (297200 at n=6), no permanent data (verified live). OEIS A089479 records permanent distributions for full n x n (0,1)-cubes through n=5 only, not the doubly-regular slice D(6,3) (verified live). General-bound literature (Csikvari proof of Friedland LMC/Schrijver; Gurvits-Leake capacity operators; Lelarge lifts; Greenhill et al. expected permanents; Federbush cluster expansion) gives lower bounds, asymptotics, or expected values, none tabulating the exact D(6,3) minimum, minimizer, or distribution. Live arXiv API query permanent+regular+bipartite (15 hits) reviewed: matching-covered/cubic-brace characterizations, invertibility, capacity, lifts, Latin counts — no D(6,3) minimum/distribution. Closest distinct invariant McKay-Wanless extremal 1-factorisation counts (decompositions into k matchings) differ from the permanent (number of perfect matchings) and do not mechanically imply m, orbits, or distribution. No prior publication of m=17, the 4-value table, or the single-orbit claim was found; the result is not a parameter substitution or database regrouping.

value.rationale: Strongest headline claim — exact minimum permanent m=17 over D(6,3) with explicit certified minimizer M*, plus the complete 4-value distribution and single minimizer orbit — is an independently retrievable exact invariant of a natural object. D(6,3) (adjacency matrices of 3-regular bipartite graphs on 6+6 vertices) was motivated before computation by Schrijver/Friedland-LMC sharpness: Schrijver gives per>=ceil((4/3)^6)=6 while Bregman gives per<=36, and the trivial all-ones extremizer is excluded by double regularity, so the exact sharpness gap (minimum 17, ratio 12393/4096) was not known or mechanically implied. A future researcher testing capacity methods, permanent approximation, or lifts could reasonably need this precise sharpness fact and the ground-truth distribution. This is a rigorously established exact datum about a motivated object, not a textbook restatement, arbitrary slice, or tiny unmotivated gain; certification strengthens but is not itself the value. Full distribution was completed and verified, so no incomplete-census discount applies.

residual_risks: Exhaustive-enumeration correctness rests on the auditor's independent re-enumeration agreeing with the candidate; a shared misreading of D(6,3) (e.g. ordered vs unlabelled) is excluded by the explicit definition and the A001501 count match, but formal proof-checker certification (e.g. DRAT-style) was not performed.
Originality rests on live OEIS/arXiv searches plus cited literature; unindexed preprints or paywalled tables with the same 4-value distribution cannot be logically excluded, though none was found.
Orbit claim is scoped to S_6 x S_6 (not quotienting by transpose), as honestly disclosed; transpose-closedness is noted separately and not part of the counted claim.
